title: SPECTRO™ 12: High-End ISTAR Performance for Smaller Platforms
summary: Advanced intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition and precision targeting are moving onto a broader range of platforms, and electro-optical payloads must deliver more within tighter size, weight and power (SWaP) limits. SPECTRO™ 12 is Elbit Systems' answer: a stabilized, 12-inch-class payload that combines multispectral imaging and precision laser designation for platforms where every kilogram, watt and centimeter matters.
body_markdown:
## **Key takeaways**


- **Compact 12-inch-class:** 25 kg multispectral EO/IR ISTAR and targeting payload, optimized for demanding SWaP constraints
- **Multispectral imaging:** visible/NIR, SWIR and MWIR thermal channels
- **Precision targeting:** laser target designation, ranging and pointing
- **Stabilized EO/IR architecture:** observation and targeting functions working as one system
- **Multi-platform integration:** UAS, light helicopters, maritime platforms and tactical ground vehicles


## **A New Weight Class for Advanced EO/IR**


For many years, more range and capability meant larger optics, more sensors and more size and weight. Today, advanced ISTAR and targeting are needed on platforms that cannot carry payloads traditionally associated with this level of performance.


“The objective behind SPECTRO 12 was to bring the advanced multispectral, targeting and processing capabilities associated with the SPECTRO family into a substantially smaller and lighter payload,” says the Head of Elbit Systems’ EO ISTAR Business Unit. “It is designed for a different class of platforms, where size, weight and power are fundamental considerations.”


## **Built on SPECTRO Heritage**


Elbit Systems has decades of experience developing stabilized electro-optical systems for airborne, maritime and land applications. Thermal detectors, multispectral observation technologies and laser systems are all developed within Elbit Systems’ electro-optics operations. Engineers can therefore optimize imaging, laser and processing as one integrated system, with alignment, performance and packaging volume tuned together. That matters most for payloads operating under tight SWaP constraints.
SPECTRO 12 builds on SPECTRO XR, the larger 15-inch-class payload, of which nearly 1,000 systems have been sold. It is not simply a smaller SPECTRO XR. It is a carefully balanced combination of multispectral observation, targeting, stabilization and processing for a significantly tighter SWaP envelope.


“Customers increasingly want advanced capabilities distributed across more platforms,”. “That puts much greater emphasis on achieving the right balance between performance, size, weight, power and cost.”


### **Full ISTAR Chain**


##
**Seeing beyond the visible**


A conventional daylight camera shows only part of the picture. SPECTRO 12 combines a 4K visible-day channel, an HD SWIR sensor and a Full-HD MWIR thermal channel within a stabilized 12-inch-class payload. This supports day and night operations across a wide range of visibility and environmental conditions.


“The purpose of the multispectral architecture is to provide the operator with different types of information from the same payload,”. “Depending on the mission and conditions, the operator can use visible imagery, SWIR or thermal information to build the operational picture.”


Working with stabilization and tracking, the sensors detect, recognize and identify objects of interest, hold line of sight as the platform moves, and generate accurate targeting information for other systems.


## **Precise designation**


##


Modern EO payloads are expected to do more than observe. SPECTRO 12 integrates a coded laser target designator, a laser rangefinder and a laser pointer with its observation channels, so compatible laser-guided weapons can home on a designated target. Designation demands very high line-of-sight accuracy, stabilization and alignment between the imaging and laser channels.


“At longer ranges, accurate laser designation requires very high line-of-sight accuracy and stabilization,”. “That is fundamentally different from simply pointing toward an area of interest.”


### **Right Sized for Every Platform**


##


**Smaller UAS and light helicopters.**


Smaller aircraft are easier to deploy in numbers, but payload weight, volume and power shrink with them. Operators have had to trade sensor capability against platform size and endurance. SPECTRO 12 brings multispectral ISTAR, precision targeting and onboard processing into this payload class without moving up to a larger aircraft. On light helicopters, it avoids the weight, integration and cost penalties of a larger EO system.


“Forces want eyes in the sky that can provide information about what is happening around them and support their operations,”. “The challenge is providing that level of capability from platforms that are becoming smaller and more widely distributed.”


## **Compact Maritime platforms**


Smaller vessels and patrol craft have had to choose between larger, higher-performance EO systems and smaller payloads with limited capability. They also contend with atmospheric effects, sea clutter and the need to hold a stable line of sight from a moving vessel. SPECTRO 12 offers another option: multispectral observation, stabilization and targeting in a package suited to smaller maritime platforms.


## **Ground applications**


##


Laser-guided weapons are spreading on tactical ground vehicles, which creates demand for compact systems that can detect, track and designate at weapon-relevant ranges. “SPECTRO 12 fits this application particularly well,”. “Its combination of capability, size and weight provides a strong balance between the ranges at which targets need to be detected and designated and the constraints of the tactical platform carrying the system.”


##


**Designed for Integration and Scale**


Elbit Systems is involved in tenders covering hundreds of units. SPECTRO 12 is progressing through platform integration, and the company is preparing its manufacturing infrastructure for anticipated production demand. “We are making a major effort around the production lines because of the needs we are seeing and the orders we expect,” says Head of Elbit Systems’ EO ISTAR Business Unit.


##
**Summary**


SPECTRO 12 was designed to make an advanced EO payload smaller. The market it serves is much larger. Sophisticated intelligence, surveillance and precision targeting are moving onto more types of platforms, including those that once could not carry payloads in this performance class. SPECTRO 12 gives them the capability they have been missing.


## **FAQ**


##


## **What is SPECTRO 12?**


SPECTRO 12 is Elbit Systems’ compact 12-inch-class multispectral EO ISTAR payload. It combines advanced observation, target acquisition, laser designation and onboard processing capabilities in a package designed for platforms with demanding size, weight and power constraints. The system draws on technology and experience from the larger SPECTRO XR while addressing a different payload and platform class.


##


**Why was SPECTRO 12 developed?**


Advanced intelligence and targeting capabilities are increasingly required on smaller and more widely distributed platforms. Light helicopters, smaller UAS, patrol vessels and tactical ground vehicles cannot always accommodate larger EO payloads. SPECTRO 12 was developed to provide a balance of multispectral capability, targeting performance and compact SWaP characteristics for these applications


##
**Does SPECTRO 12 Include Laser Designation?**


Yes. SPECTRO 12 combines its observation sensors with a coded laser target designator, laser rangefinder and laser pointer. This enables the payload to combine observation and target acquisition with precision laser designation for compatible laser-guided weapons.


##


**Which Platforms Is SPECTRO 12 Designed for?**


SPECTRO 12 is intended for smaller and medium UAS, light helicopters, maritime vessels and tactical ground vehicles, particularly applications where payload weight, volume and power consumption are a significant integration constraints
